title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on Private/VPC pilot network issues and upgrade plan. Confirmed routing fixes, validated connectivity for inference workers, reviewed preliminary benchmark numbers (latency/throughput), discussed KMS integration and audit logging, agreed on a Sunday maintenance window for model runtime upgrade. Next: Maya to send updated network diagram, Carlos to run a full 24h load test and share results, Lina to provide NAT/GW logs and approve maintenance window.
topics: model runtime upgrade and kernel selection

Lina: provide NAT gateway flow logs and VPC peering config by 2026-06-26

Schedule Sunday maintenance window for runtime upgrade (proposed 2026-06-28 02:00-05:00 UTC)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Nora (Redwood CSM), Rajesh (CTO PulseHealth), Lina (DevOps), Tom (InfoSec), Aisha (SRE)
Shared: network-diagram-v1.pdf, initial-benchmarks-2026-06-20.csv

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, afternoon in UTC, uh let's do a quick round robin, real quick status updates before we dive into the routing stuff.
00:18 Rajesh: hey Maya, thanks. Quick from us — overall the inference work looks good but we hit some intermittent failures during the morning load tests, mostly connection resets, so we're blocked on running full end-to-end.
00:30 Carlos: okay yeah we saw that too in the logs, looked like occasional NAT gateway issues combined with stale route caches on the worker nodes.
00:42 Lina: yep, we pulled flow logs, there's a pattern where some egress IPs were being SNAT'd differently after scaling events. We'll share the raw flows.
00:55 Maya: appreciated. Carlos, can you remind the group what the architecture is for the private deployment — just short?
01:05 Carlos: sure — private control plane on Redwood side, customer VPC with dedicated inference hosts in the private subnet, we do VPC peering and route announcements to the workers, KV cache and prefix cache kept locally on the hosts. We also recommend a NAT or egress gateway for model downloads and container registry pulls.
01:28 Aisha: quick question — when you say VPC peering, are you using AWS peering or transit gateway in your recommendation? Because we prefer not to create a dozen peering connections.
01:39 Carlos: good call — for scale we usually recommend TGW, agreed. For the pilot we set up a simple peering to move faster but TGW is the plan for prod.
01:50 Tom: from security, the thing we care about is KMS integration and audit logs, so any manual fixes that change routes need to be visible in the log stream. SOC2 auditors will want the full chain.
02:05 Maya: understood — we can include the audit/logging plan in the playbook. We'll need to double-check retention windows too.
02:12 Tom: yep, 3 years retention for some signals is our baseline, plus ability to export to S3.
02:20 Nora: quick note — we already have a draft playbook, attaching network-diagram-v2.pdf in the notes after this call.
02:30 Lina: thanks. Okay about the morning resets — we cross referenced with the worker autoscaler events, and there are a few roll events at 03:12 that correlate. The nodes rejoined and acquired new ENIs which changed SNAT behavior.
02:46 Carlos: that explains it — if the node reattaches with a different IP, and the NAT mapping hasn't warmed the upstream firewall, you can get transient drops. We can add sticky SNAT or preserve source IPs with a NAT gateway.
03:00 Rajesh: is that something urgent? It blocks our nightly sync jobs which run heavy throughput tests.
03:08 Carlos: not urgent, but needs a config tweak. We can walk Lina through adjusting the autoscaler lifecycle hooks to drain properly and ensure ENI attachments are stable during scale.
03:20 Lina: I can do that, but will need the exact command snippets or terraform changes — can you provide a PR or patch?
03:29 Maya: yes — we'll include terraform snippet in the playbook.
03:33 Tom: also to note — when you did the initial kernel upgrade last week, do you have an artifact of which CUDA/CUDNN combos you validated? Our security needs to know the exact runtime versions to lock down drivers.
03:46 Carlos: we tested runtime v2.1.3 with CUDA 12.1 and cuDNN 9.0 on the A10 GPUs in your env; there was a fallback to quantized kernels for lower memory configs. I'll put the exact matrix in the doc.
04:00 Rajesh: perfect. On benchmarks: your initial-benchmarks-2026-06-20.csv shows median latency ~85ms but 99p spikes up to 620ms during concurrent requests. Is that expected for the Private setup?
04:20 Carlos: the 99p spikes line up with cache misses and repeated model loads — we found the KV cache wasn't warmed for some prefixes during the morning burst. Also batching behavior under varied sequence lengths can create bursts.
04:37 Aisha: what's our target 99p? For product we want under 250ms ideally.
04:44 Maya: that's a reasonable target, we'll aim for <250ms 99p for the pilot. In dedicated you'd see better P99.
04:53 Lina: can Redwood change the cache TTL or pre-warm prefixes?
04:58 Carlos: yes — we can pre-warm top 100 prefixes and adjust KV cache TTL. We also recommended using our prefix caching layer in persistent mode for the pilot.
05:12 Rajesh: ok let's do that. Next — model runtime upgrade you mentioned in the ticket, what's the risk window?
05:21 Maya: we propose a small rolling upgrade window Sunday 02:00-05:00 UTC. We'll do canary on 10% of hosts then ramp. There are rollback steps documented.
05:36 Tom: will that break in-flight requests? We need graceful drain to avoid dropped inference requests.
05:42 Carlos: we'll enable stream-aware drain and wait for in-flight token streams to complete, plus a short grace period. There will be some latency increase during canary but not errors if done correctly.
05:55 Lina: we need the exact drain command and healthcheck path to integrate with our autoscaler.
06:02 Carlos: noted, will add in playbook.
06:05 Rajesh: on the licensing/competitors side — any differences we should be aware of comparing to Bedrock or Anthropic hosted options? We care about control of data and locality.
06:18 Maya: main difference is you keep control of the VPC and data flow in Private deployment; hosted options like Bedrock offload infra but you hand over egress and data flow. Costs and latency profiles differ.
06:30 Tom: good. Also, we need to confirm the KMS key rotation patterns — if Redwood calls KMS in the customer's account, what permissions are required?
06:41 Carlos: typically decrypt and generate-data-key-permission for the service principal plus a small set of IAM permissions; we'll provide an IAM policy.
06:50 Tom: send policy please.
06:53 Maya: action item.
07:00 Maya: okay let's review the log snippets you sent earlier — Lina, can you share the specific NAT flow lines?
07:06 Lina: sure pasted in slack, but quick excerpt shows TCP resets followed by re-syn attempts, port ranges consistent with SNAT.
07:18 Carlos: so immediate mitigation: route sticky SNAT or central NAT gateway; longer-term: TGW and stable ENI attachments and lifecycle hooks.
07:30 Rajesh: can we try sticky SNAT as a short-term measure and schedule moving to TGW?
07:36 Lina: yes we can try sticky SNAT tomorrow, I'll patch and monitor.
07:41 Maya: excellent. Now on benchmarks, Carlos you mentioned a planned 24h test — what's in scope?
07:48 Carlos: we'll run a sustained mixed workload with production-like sequence lengths, include cold-starts to capture KV cache miss behavior, and measure median, p95, p99 latency and throughput. We'll also capture GPU utilization and memory pressure.
08:02 Aisha: capture CPU steal or host throttling too, that affected us last month.
08:10 Carlos: noted. We'll also include model variant fallback tests to ensure graceful fallback to lower-precision quantized variants.
08:20 Rajesh: how will we share results? CSV + Grafana link?
08:25 Carlos: yes CSV upload and short summary slide; we'll post link to shared drive and slack.
08:31 Maya: timeline for that was next Monday/Tuesday? You had said by 6/29 in the ticket.
08:36 Carlos: that's right, 24h run starting 6/27 and finish 6/28, analyze 6/29.
08:42 Lina: operational question: who will perform the model runtime upgrade? We prefer Redwood to execute since it's sensitive and you're more familiar.
08:50 Maya: we can do it, with your approval and a runbook. We'll request elevated access for the maintenance window and run it collaborately with your SREs.
08:59 Tom: we will require a pre-signed JIRA change request and cross-team sign-off before window.
09:06 Maya: that's fine. We'll create the change request and tag compliance.
09:10 Rajesh: any outstanding blockers?
09:13 Lina: NAT flows and confirming the drain healthcheck path — after that most of the functional blockers cleared. The rest is validation.
09:22 Carlos: one more note — we found a kernel match issue on one of the older AMIs which caused suboptimal kernel selection for attention layers; after forcing the optimized kernel selection latency improved by ~20%. We'll include exact kernel flags.
09:39 Rajesh: good to know. Please include the patch.
09:43 Carlos: will do.
09:45 Maya: quick recap — action items we've recorded (see notes). Proposed maintenance window Sunday 02-05 UTC. Network diagram v2 and terraform snippets by Friday (6/26). Carlos runs 24h load test and shares results by 6/29. Lina to provide NAT logs by 6/26. Tom to confirm SOC2 fields by 6/28.
10:10 Tom: about audit logs — will Redwood ship logs to our S3 bucket or do you expect us to pull them?
10:19 Nora: we can push to your S3 via cross-account role; otherwise you can set up an exporter. Pushing is simplest.
10:27 Tom: ensure encryption-in-transit and server-side encryption enabled.
10:31 Nora: yes — SSE-KMS recommended; we support that.
10:35 Rajesh: anything else?
10:38 Maya: final check — competitors or procurement questions for the week?
10:42 Rajesh: not really, procurement asked for a revised price estimate if we move to TGW/dedicated capacity — could you provide that after the pilot?
10:53 Maya: yes we'll follow up.
10:56 Rajesh: ok thanks all. Let's meet same time next week.
11:00 Maya: great, thanks everyone. I'll send notes and the network diagram.
11:05 END
